pr.title: Hear a microphone through its track while it records: field record --monitoring host (live-supercollider.md chunk 4)
pr.head: baca45ebea364e47ff3787a4a4b5f00e78962340

summary: Field records a microphone through field record: the daemon, field-audiod, opens the interface's input channel, writes it to a crash-safe take, and plays the song as the bed you perform against. Until this change you never heard the microphone through Field itself. --monitoring only wrote a label on the take's row, and you listened through your interface's own mixer, which this project calls Apollo-direct monitoring after the Universal Audio interface it was designed around.

This pull request makes field record --monitoring host play each armed audio track's input through that track's inserts, the buses above it, and main, from arming through the count-in and the take. The take itself stays the dry input. The default stays apollo-direct, which plays nothing of the input.

It reuses the path that the live-supercollider plan's chunks 1 to 3 built for field keys. A song's session can carry an input window: a slot on a track that plays a live input, a source outside the song, through that track's chain and every chain above it. field keys feeds an input window from a shared-memory ring. This change adds a second kind of live input, a capture input, which reads one channel straight from the audio callback's own input block.

1. Refuse what cannot be heard. Before arming, field record compiles the song with the capture inputs it is about to open, and refuses a track the song cannot hear.
  2. Arm with a name. field record arms each audio track with monitor: "capture:<song>/<track>", and the daemon opens a capture input under that name, owned by the connection that armed.
  3. Reload the song with it. field record loads the song again with an input window naming the capture input, keeping the loaded session's loop, region, and solo.
  4. Read it each callback. Before the session renders a block, the daemon hands the callback's input block to every capture input, which reads its channel from it.
  5. Tear down. When the take ends, or anything throws after the arm, field record disarms, which closes the capture inputs, and loads the song again without them while the daemon still plays it. A dropped connection also closes them.

cards.title: Terms
cards.html:
• Live input: a source outside the song that an input window plays, read once per block on the audio thread (LiveInput).
  • Input window: a slot on a track in the compiled session that names a live input.
  • Capture input: the new live input, reading one armed channel from the callback's input block (CaptureInput).
  • Ring: the shared-memory buffer that carries a field keys voice from SuperCollider to the daemon.
  • Overlay: the second instance of each track's chain that carries live inputs up to main, beside the rendered song.
  • Converted delivery: the daemon resampling the song to a device that cannot run at the song's rate.

cards.title: Review so far
cards.html:
The first review, of f4f8f47, opened three findings in src/commands/record.ts. baca45e fixes all three, and the second review verified each fix:

  • A track the loaded solo or the arrangement keeps from main is now refused before arming.
  • A device rate the song is not, opened by the arm, is now refused after arming, and the arm is released.
  • The reload after a take now runs only while the daemon still plays the take's song.

The second review opened three findings of its own:

  • A refused arm still reloads the song, which ends another terminal's loop take.
  • The plan says every gap has a test, but nothing covers the rate refusal.
  • One edited line in docs/audio-engine.md breaks the paragraph's wrapping.

Tests ran on the daemon's null device only. Criterion 6, hearing a real microphone through headphones, is owed on hardware.

cards.title: Left for later
cards.html:
• The latency policy in docs/audio-engine.md "Latency" is not built. What you hear is late by the input and output buffers plus the limiters and hosted plugins on the path.
  • Converted delivery is refused rather than resampled.
  • Monitoring without a take waits for arming.md chunk 3's lasting field arm.

groups.title: The arm and status contract
groups.kicker: What crosses the socket: a monitor name on an armed track, and capture inputs in status.
intro: The CLI and the daemon agree on three additions. An audio entry in arm's tracks list may carry monitor, the name of the capture input to open. status.inputs, which listed only field keys rings, now also lists capture inputs as {name, kind: "capture", read, peak}. The daemon advertises the live-monitor feature, so an older daemon gets a clear refusal.
The server passes the connection to armSet as the capture inputs' owner, which is how a dropped field record connection closes them.

groups.title: The capture input
groups.kicker: A second kind of live input that reads one channel of the callback's own input block.
intro: CaptureBlock holds the callback's input for the block in progress: its channel pointers, their count, and the frame count. CaptureInput is a LiveInput that reads one channel of that block onto both sides.

The session can read a block in more than one step, because it splits a block where a loop wraps. So the capture input keeps a cursor into the block, and starts the cursor again whenever the block's generation changes. A read past the block's end, a channel the block does not hold, or a closed input reads silence.
field-audiod --capture-selftest checks those cases without a device.

files.note: CaptureBlock, which the audio thread alone presents, reads, and clears, and CaptureInput, whose close() the message thread calls.

checks.text: Every caller of present, clear, and read runs on the callback's thread inside liveLock's try-lock, and every locate turns input reads off (overlayReadsInputs), so these plain fields have one thread. Traced through renderOverlay's callers in live.cpp.

files.note: The read, the counters status shows, and the self-test.

checks.text: In steady state the session reads exactly the callback's frame count from each input per block, so the cursor neither pads nor drops. The step loop splits only at a wrap, and the limiter and hosted plugins emit as much as they take in once primed. Traced through LiveSession::renderBlock.
Ran field-audiod --capture-selftest on a Release build of this head: it printed {"ok":true}.

groups.title: The player opens, feeds, and closes capture inputs
groups.kicker: Where armSet opens capture inputs, the callback feeds them, and disarm or a dropped connection closes them.
intro: Player keeps capture inputs in a captures map beside the rings map, under the same lock, and a session load hands both to the new session.

armSet validates each monitor: a MIDI track has no input to monitor, two tracks cannot share a name, and a ring cannot already hold it. It opens the capture inputs only after nothing else in the arm can fail, replacing the previous arm's. disarm, a dropped connection, and quit close them.

In pullAudio, the callback presents its input block before the session renders and clears it afterwards. Under converted delivery it presents nothing, because the session then renders in session-rate steps that are not this block's frames.

files.note: The captures map's lifecycle, the present-and-clear around the render, and capture inputs in status.

checks.text: Under converted delivery the capture inputs read silence. field record refuses host monitoring when status.resampling is set before arming, and again after arming when the arm opened the device at a rate the song is not.
closeCaptures() runs after the last failure point in armSet, so a refused arm keeps the previous arm's capture inputs, as the method's comment promises for the rest of the arm.
A dropped connection closes the capture inputs it opened and leaves the arm. live-monitor.test.ts checks both, and it passed on this head.

files.note: Declares captures, captureBlock, closeCaptures, and the new owner argument to armSet.

groups.title: Every reload keeps both kinds of live input
groups.kicker: One helper lists the open live inputs for a song, so every command that reloads it keeps them.
intro: When any command loads a song's session again, it must compile in the live inputs that are open for that song, or their input windows vanish and the voice or microphone goes silent. Chunk 3 did that for field keys rings with keysInputsFor.

This change moves that helper to src/audiod/live-inputs.ts as liveInputsFor, which matches both keys: and capture: names. Beside it sit compileWithInputs, which compiles the song as a reload would, reloadWithInputs, which loads that compile and keeps the session's loop, region, and solo, and reloadIfPlaying, which reloads only while the daemon still plays the song. field keys and field record share them. field play, its watch, and field ui switch to liveInputsFor with no other change.

files.note: liveInputsFor, captureInputName, compileWithInputs, reloadWithInputs, and reloadIfPlaying.

checks.text: compileWithInputs compiles the song as a reload would: with the open inputs plus any extra, under the loaded session's loop and solo. field record calls it before arming, so a track the song cannot hear is refused before the input opens.

reloadIfPlaying reloads only while the daemon is live on song, so a song another terminal loaded meanwhile plays on. It does not check whether a take is recording; field keys' close checks that itself, and field record's finally does not.
Song directories are one path segment and track names are slugs, so the regular expression splits every name a project allows. t.node.trackName is the same key compileSession looks tracks up by.

files.note: Uses the shared reloadWithInputs, and reloadIfPlaying on quit and after a failed route, so it leaves a song another terminal loaded.
keysInputsFor becomes liveInputsFor for the load and the watch.
keysInputsFor becomes liveInputsFor for the load, solo swaps, and the watch.

groups.title: field record --monitoring host
groups.kicker: The CLI flow: refuse what cannot be heard, arm with names, reload, and put the song back.
intro: --monitoring host was already accepted as a label for the take's row. Now it also drives monitoring. Before arming, field record refuses when no named track records audio, when the daemon predates live-monitor, when the bed is a file, when the daemon plays another song, and when the daemon converts the song to the device's rate. It also compiles the song with the capture inputs it is about to open, and refuses a track that a solo, a muted placement, or the arrangement keeps from main.

It then always arms in the tracks form, even for one track, so it can name each audio track's capture input. After arming it refuses when the arm opened the device at a rate the song is not, which a separate input device can do. Otherwise it reloads the song with every open input.
The function's outer finally now releases the arm whatever throws after it, and reloads the song without the capture inputs while the daemon still plays it.

files.note: The refusals before and after arming, monitor on each audio entry, the reload, and the finally that releases the arm.

checks.text: armedHere turns true before armTracks returns, so when the daemon refuses the arm because another terminal's take is recording, the finally still runs reloadIfPlaying. The swap drops the other take's region, so a loop take stops wrapping. Reproduced on the null daemon; at f4f8f47 the loop take kept wrapping.
A session soloed on another track, and a track not placed in main, are refused here before arming, with record.state left idle. Reproduced on the null daemon.

armedRate is the device's rate from armSet, and rate is status.sample_rate, which under a live session is the song's rate, so the comparison catches an arm that switched the device. Verified by reading; no null-device test can reach it.
With tall-grass loaded by another client mid-take, the reload here leaves tall-grass playing. Reproduced on the null daemon.
The capture input's name is capture:<song>/<track>, the shape liveInputsFor matches.

files.note: The --monitoring help text names host.
A comment on monitoring names host.

groups.title: Tests
groups.kicker: The daemon's capture inputs, and field record end to end, on the null device.
intro: The null device's input 1 is a sawtooth that reaches full scale once a second, and its input 2 is a constant 0.25. A capture input's peak near 1 therefore proves it read input 1, and a gapless sawtooth in a landed take proves the take is the dry input.

checks.text: Ran live-monitor.test.ts, record-daemon.test.ts, routing.test.ts, live-input.test.ts, and live-session.test.ts on the null device at this head: 42 of 42 passed. No native file changed since f4f8f47, so they ran against that head's daemon build.

files.note: The daemon alone: read while stopped and while playing, closed by disarm and by a dropped connection, and the three refusals.
field record --monitoring host end to end, the solo and off-main refusals before arming, a song another terminal loads mid-take, and the file-bed refusal.
